sectionHeading: Indigenous Governance: Coordination Around the Living World
currentHeading: Indigenous Governance: Accountability to Place and Descendants
authority: Editorial craft owned by the editorial agent under author delegation. Consent, attribution, and reciprocity obligations belong to the author and to CTD-0069.

ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0069 governs this section and is an open obligation rather than a ruling, so it does not override the baseline. One sentence of the shipped text is kept because it serves the item directly: that these traditions are diverse and cannot be treated as one system. CTD-0008 explicitly routes the consent and accountable-lineage questions here to CTD-0069, and neither is discharged by this restoration. The word indigenous is capitalized throughout, which is orthography rather than a claim change.

findings.summary: The section's statement of what Providence inherits was removed, leaving a lesson without an heir.

evidence.baseline: This is the ancestor of Providence's deepest ecological and temporal commitments: the orientation toward those not yet born, the treatment of the living world as the first participant rather than the backdrop, the long-horizon stewardship that the Currency of Presence is meant to make economically coordinable.
evidence.shipped: Providence draws from this lesson with caution.

findings.authorizedBy: Compression, and the wave-one caution about appropriating traditions.
findings.diagnosis: The three commitments named here are the volume's dedication, the volume's ecological chapters, and the volume's currency, in that order. Naming them is what makes the acknowledgment specific rather than ceremonial: it says exactly which parts of the design descend from these traditions, which is a precondition of the accountable attribution CTD-0069 asks for. Draws from this lesson with caution names nothing and therefore attributes nothing.

findings.summary: The acknowledgment of suppression was cut down and lost its subject.

evidence.baseline: it is drawn from peoples whose knowledge was, in many cases, violently suppressed by the very institutions whose failures this book catalogues, and ... the respectful learning from these traditions must never become another act of extraction from them.
evidence.shipped: Learning must not become another extraction from peoples whose lands and knowledge have already been taken.

findings.diagnosis: The shipped sentence keeps the prohibition and drops the connection: that the institutions which suppressed this knowledge are the same ones Chapter Three examined. Have already been taken has no agent. The baseline names the agent as the book's own subject matter, which is the harder and more accountable sentence.

findings.summary: One prohibited mark, introducing a three-item specification.

evidence.baseline: Providence's deepest ecological and temporal commitments.

findings.diagnosis: It became a colon. The three items specify what the commitments are.

debtImpact.note: Restoring the named inheritance improves attribution, which the item asks for. The shipped sentence acknowledging that the traditions are diverse and not one system is kept for the same reason. Consent, relationship, and material reciprocity remain entirely owed, and the restored text makes the claim larger rather than smaller.

Perhaps its most important lesson, and one the modern world has been catastrophically slow to learn, returns, as does the claim about what many such traditions encode in their structures of deliberation.
Indigenous governance traditions across the world is an unbounded generalization about a category of enormous internal variety.

generations.label: A
generations.title: Derived from baseline under the standard, the corpus card, and the volume card

reasoning.note: The full statement of the lesson, the account of accountability to descendants and to land and water, the three named inheritances, and the acknowledgment of suppression with the connection to Chapter Three.
One sentence from the shipped text: these traditions are diverse and cannot be treated as one system. CTD-0069 asks for exactly this bound and the baseline does not supply it.
indigenous became Indigenous throughout. Orthography, not claim.
The rest of the shipped rewrite.

openQuestions: Attribution. The restoration makes the volume's debt to Indigenous governance larger and more specific than the shipped text did, and it does so without naming a single people, nation, or source. CTD-0069's consent, relationship, and reciprocity obligations are therefore more pressing after this change than before it. This is the one restoration in the chapter that the author may reasonably want reversed until the item is paid.

Heading. Coordination Around the Living World is the phrase the section's argument uses. Accountability to Place and Descendants names two of the three inheritances. Not changed. Renaming costs a section id and a recorded route alias in publishing/continuity.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the stored text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, editorial/sources/corpus/voice-card.md, the volume-03 voice card, the master ledger, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required, but this section is the clearest case in the volume where restoring the baseline increases an outstanding obligation rather than merely reopening it. The instruction was to restore and flag, which was followed, and the flag is stronger here than elsewhere: a fuller claim of inheritance from living peoples is a larger debt to them, not a smaller one.
